column1: # The settings grammar, one sample per row, read by BOTH sides:
# `settings_template::read` over the sample as a template, and the real
# the sample as a consumer's kendex.settings.toml. A row's verdict is what
# the loaders do; the reader must report a finding for every row the
# loaders will not read as written, and none for a row they read cleanly.
# Add a row here and both sides are held to it.
# So a rule only a TEMPLATE has cannot live here, however much it looks
# like grammar. The loaders have no opinion on a comment block over every
# key, on an assignment outside [env], or on where the `# required` marker
# sits, and a row asserting one would say the reader and the loaders
# disagree — which is the one thing this corpus exists to refuse. Those are
# The leading-bom row carries the three BOM bytes literally, in the body
# field where no reader of this file can mistake them for a header: it is
# the one encoding the shell harness and the Rust side read identically,
# since neither unescapes the other's octal or unicode spelling.
#   loads    the loaders load the file and export KEY as EXPECT ("quoted";
#            a tab-separated field is never left empty)
#   refused  the loaders fail the whole file loud
#   unread   the loaders load the file and never export KEY
